description: Run a program with secrets from SEAL links or your inbox in its environment. The values never enter this conversation: they are removed from the output you get back. Use it instead of reading a secret file. With no secrets the program runs under this machine's guard: the keys it holds are put in only at their hosts.

command.description: The program and its arguments, run without a shell.

cwd.description: Working directory of the program; default this server's.

secrets.description: Each one is a link or an inbox item with one text file, up to 64 KiB, put into one variable of the program's environment. An empty list runs the program under this machine's guard alone, with stand-ins of the keys it holds.

item.description: An inbox handle from seal_inbox (`in_…`), instead of a URL.

name.description: The variable; default: the file's name in capitals (`Brave API key` → `BRAVE_API_KEY`), `SEAL_<NAME>` when that name steers a program (`PATH`, `NODE_OPTIONS`, …). The result's `vars` says which variable each secret filled.

password.description: The password of a protected seal, when the user said it in this conversation; otherwise `password_file`.

password_file.description: Path of a file whose first line is the seal's password: the path seal_request returns for kind=secret. Not together with `password`. A run takes one password: secrets of different passwords go in calls of their own.

url.description: The full SEAL link, with everything after `#` when it has it.

timeout.description: Seconds; after them the program is killed.

name: seal_run
title: Run a program with secrets
